note: Curated inputs for scripts/derive-costs.ts. Each figure is copied from the source named beside it. Rents per square metre and electricity prices are turned into monthly costs with the app assumptions below; other values are used as they are. Re-run the script after changing anything.

assumptions.description: App assumptions, not measured data: typical floor area and yearly household electricity use (not heating) by number of bedrooms.

dwelling.1: two-room flat (one bedroom and a living room)
dwelling.2: flat of three or more rooms
dwelling.3: flat of three or more rooms
dwelling.4: flat of three or more rooms

rent.limitations: Average rent per m² of new privately financed leases (Statistics Finland table 15fa); three-or-more-room flats share one figure. Heating is normally included; water and electricity are not.

waterPerPerson.basis: HSY water and wastewater fees for 2026 (€4.67 per m³ with VAT) at 130 litres a person a day; Motiva gives 90 to 270 litres, used for the range.
waterPerPerson.limitations: Landlords often bill water as a flat fee per resident, which can differ from metered cost.

transitPassAdult.basis: HSL 30-day season ticket, zones AB; the saver subscription costs €61.60.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Finland (€759.66 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

observation.basis: Municipal early-education fee from 1 August 2026: 10.7% of monthly gross household income above a threshold for the family size, at most €335 for the youngest child; under €32 nothing is charged. The second child pays 40% and each further child 20% of the youngest child's fee.
observation.limitations: Uses gross wage income only and counts children under 17 in the family size (the rule counts children under 18). Families of more than six use the threshold for six. Part-time care costs less.

dwelling.1: flat of any size (net cold rent)
dwelling.2: flat of any size (net cold rent)
dwelling.3: flat of any size (net cold rent)
dwelling.4: flat of any size (net cold rent)

rent.limitations: Median asking rent per m² across all advertised flats in Berlin (IBB Wohnungsmarktbericht 2025, 40,014 listings); no split by size. Net cold rent: operating costs and heating are added under utilities.

operatingCostsPerM2.basis: Operating costs billed to tenants in Germany, Betriebskostenspiegel for 2024 (Deutscher Mieterbund): the sum of all cost types, €3.31 per m² a month, including heating, hot water and water; €2.89 without lift, garden care and cable.

transitPassAdult.basis: Deutschlandticket, valid on all local transport in Germany; €66.80 from January 2027.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Germany (€702.63 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

childcarePerChild.basis: Kita places in Berlin are free; parents pay a €23 meal contribution. Providers may charge up to €100 more a month for extras.
childcarePerChild.limitations: Covers public and subsidised places; a place is not guaranteed at a particular Kita.

rent.limitations: Average asking rent per m² on idealista for the city of Madrid in September 2026; districts range from about €17 to €28.5. Existing leases are much lower (€12.8 per m² in 2022, Ministry of Housing reference index).

waterPerPerson.basis: Average water and sanitation cost in the Community of Madrid in 2024 (€1.74 per m³) at the measured average use of 128 litres a person a day (INE).

transitPassAdult.basis: 30-day public transport pass, zone A, at the 2026 discounted price (Consorcio Regional de Transportes, BOCM 31 Dec 2025).

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Spain (€647.45 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

childcarePerChild.basis: Public nursery schools (0–3) in the Community of Madrid: tuition is free; meals cost €96 a month.
childcarePerChild.limitations: Public places are limited; private nurseries charge tuition, which is not included.

rentObservations.limitations: HUD Fair Market Rents for FY2026, Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos metro area: the 40th percentile of gross rents paid by recent movers, including utilities except phone and internet. Checked against HUD's FY2026 documentation page for Travis County on 2026-10-20; FY2027 (from October 2026) is $1,817 for two bedrooms.

transitPassAdult.basis: CapMetro calendar-month pass for local and rapid buses; fares rise on 10 January 2027.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Employer health plan: the average worker share of a single-coverage premium ($1,440 a year, KFF 2025) plus out-of-pocket spending per person ($556.6 billion in 2024, CMS, over 340.0 million people).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: Assumes an employer plan. Without one, marketplace premiums are much higher; family coverage costs the worker about $6,850 a year.

childcarePerChild.basis: Average price of centre-based infant care in Texas ($11,349 a year; toddlers $10,921), Child Care Aware of America.
childcarePerChild.limitations: A Texas average; Austin prices are likely higher.

carMonthly.basis: Average cost of owning and running a new car in the US, including depreciation, finance, fuel and insurance, at 15,000 miles a year (AAA Your Driving Costs 2025).
carMonthly.limitations: A new-car national average; an older car costs less.

transitPassAdult.basis: Urban bus fare of 9 pesos (kept by Sonora's transport institute in August 2025) for 44 rides a month; 60 rides for the range. There is no monthly pass.
transitPassAdult.limitations: Assumes two rides a working day.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Out-of-pocket health spending per person in Mexico (US$313.80 in 2023, World Bank) at the 2023 average exchange rate (17.74 pesos per dollar).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average. Salaried workers are covered by IMSS, but many people also pay for private care.
